subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw’s web-tool egress boundary be a scoped `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, a managed-proxy-owned policy, or a cross-tool allow/deny domain policy covering fetch and search?
rationale: This is an operator-trusted security boundary and the open related PRs embody different product/security answers that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
options.body: Review the open hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while leaving denied domains and generic search coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy The Boundary
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config work and route app-owned egress control through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require Cross-Tool Design
options.body: Ask for a design covering `web_fetch`, managed/native `web_search`, provider fallback, redirects, cache keys, proxy behavior, and deny semantics before code lands.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
recommendation.body: Review the open hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while leaving denied domains and generic search coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent signal across Codex search config, SSRF hardening, and the open hostname allowlist direction.
